title: Polymer clay double-ended bookmark
subtitle: A double-ended page marker with a sculpted clay charm on each end, joined by a ribbon
excerpt: Two small polymer clay charms , a mushroom and a leaf, each about 25 mm tall , are baked and then strung onto a ribbon that sits over the top edge of a book page, holding the bookmark in place without a hook. The double-ended design is heavier than a standard ribbon bookmark and stays put even in thick books.
sourceNotes: Polymer clay double-ended bookmark derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: A PVC-based modelling clay that cures hard at 110-130°C in a domestic oven
Kneading polymer clay until warm and pliable before shaping

content.text: This bookmark drapes over the top of a book page so both charms hang down one on each side. A 25 cm length of narrow ribbon holds the two ends. The mushroom charm and leaf charm are sculpted separately, each with a tunnel bored through the top for the ribbon before baking. Post-bake the assembly takes minutes.

items.name: Polymer clay, red or orange for mushroom cap

content.text: . Roll a short cylinder for the stem , 10 mm diameter and 15 mm tall. Flare the bottom slightly by pressing it on the work surface.
Condition the red clay. Roll a ball 15 mm in diameter, flatten it into a dome for the cap. Press the dome flat-side-down onto the top of the stem.
Add small dots of cream clay to the red cap to make the spots. Press gently to flatten slightly.

While still soft, bore a hole through the top of the mushroom from front to back, just below the cap edge, using the needle tool. The hole must be large enough for the ribbon to pass through , thread the ribbon through to test before baking.

Condition the green clay. Roll a ball of about 10 g and press it into a leaf shape , a teardrop flattened to about 4 mm thick, 20 mm wide, and 30 mm long. Pinch a defined point at the narrow end (leaf tip). Pinch a flat stem at the wide end.
Score veins into the leaf surface with the needle tool: a central vein from stem to tip, and angled side veins every 5 mm.
Bore the ribbon hole through the stem end before baking. Thread the ribbon through to check the fit.
Bake both charms at 130°C for 20 minutes on baking paper. Allow to cool.

Thread one end of the ribbon through the mushroom ribbon hole and tie a small knot to prevent the charm from sliding off. Thread the other end through the leaf hole and knot. The ribbon loop between the two charms should be about 20 cm , enough to sit over a book edge with both charms visible.
Optionally, apply one coat of clear varnish to each charm for added durability.

items.solution: Thread a short length of wire through the hole during baking to hold it open, then remove after cooling.
Thin sections with weak joins are the usual cause. Ensure the stem is a solid piece; press all joins securely before baking.
